title: Attention Is All You Need
research_problem: Existing sequence transduction models rely on recurrent or convolutional neural networks, which enforce sequential computation and limit parallelization, especially for long sequences.
main_contribution: Introduce the Transformer, a novel architecture that eliminates recurrence and convolutions entirely, relying solely on attention mechanisms to capture global dependencies, resulting in higher translation quality, greater parallelism, and substantially reduced training time.
methodology: Encoder‑decoder architecture built from stacked self‑attention and point‑wise feed‑forward layers
Scaled dot‑product attention and multi‑head attention to capture dependencies at multiple representation subspaces
Parameter‑free positional encoding to inject order information
Training on eight P100 GPUs for as little as twelve hours
Encoder‑decoder architecture for sequence transduction
Stacked self‑attention layers in both encoder and decoder
Point‑wise fully connected feed‑forward networks
Residual connections around each sub‑layer
Layer normalization after each residual connection
Scaled Dot‑Product Attention (softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V)
Multi‑Head Attention (parallel attention heads with linear projections)
Masking in decoder self‑attention to prevent attending to subsequent positions
Use h = 8 parallel attention heads with dk = dv = dmodel/h = 64
Apply multi-head attention in three ways: encoder-decoder attention, encoder self-attention, decoder self-attention with masking to preserve auto-regressive property
Each encoder and decoder layer includes a position-wise feed-forward network: FFN(x) = max(0, xW1 + b1)W2 + b2, with dmodel = 512 and inner dimension dff = 2048
Learned token embeddings of dimension dmodel are shared with the pre-softmax linear transformation; embedding weights are scaled by √dmodel
Add sinusoidal positional encodings to input embeddings: PE(pos,2i) = sin(pos/10000^{2i/dmodel}), PE(pos,2i+1) = cos(pos/10000^{2i/dmodel})
Also experimented with learned positional embeddings, yielding nearly identical results
Self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when sequence length n < representation dimensionality d.
Restricting self-attention to a neighborhood of size r increases maximum path length to O(n/r).

A single convolutional layer with kernel width k < n does not connect all input-output positions; a stack of O(n/k) convolutional layers (contiguous kernels) or O(log_k(n)) layers (dilated convolutions) is required.
Convolutional layers are generally more expensive than recurrent layers by a factor of k.
Separable convolutions reduce complexity to O(k·n·d + n·d^2).
With k = n, the complexity of a separable convolution equals that of a self-attention layer plus a point-wise feed-forward layer.
results: Achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English‑German translation task ( >2 BLEU improvement over previous best) and 41.8 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English‑French task after 3.5 days of training on eight GPUs; also establishes state‑of‑the‑art performance on English constituency parsing.
limitations: Self-attention becomes less efficient for very long sequences.
Convolutional layers are more expensive than recurrent layers by a factor of k.
future_work: Investigate restricting self-attention to a neighborhood of size r to improve computational performance for very long sequences.
